brief: The Fed raised rates 25bp to 3.75-4.00%, backed unanimously by all twelve voters, its first hike in over three years. Updated forecasts point to one more hike this year and open the door to a 2027 hike, more hawkish than SEB expected; combined with Fed Governor Warsh's press-conference remarks, this challenges SEB's base case of a single hike to shore up Fed credibility. SEB now sees energy prices and their pass-through to other prices as decisive for the path ahead, though an October hike, days before the midterms, looks less likely. The market reaction was hawkish: short-end rates rose more than long-end, the dollar strengthened, and the S&P 500 (-0.5%) and Nasdaq (-0.01%) reversed from gains to close lower, despite stronger-than-expected August retail sales earlier that day. Oil eased to $105.6/bbl on reduced supply-disruption concern after reports Saudi Arabia rerouted more output via Oman and the previously attacked East-West pipeline, even as the Middle East conflict widened with Saudi strikes on Yemen and Houthi attacks on Saudi cities. Sweden's Riksbank survey shows energy costs hitting firms without spurring outsized pass-through pricing, while consumption still rose in July despite weak confidence.
